analysis.title: The bill comes due - Monthly Outlook
key_insights: Rabobank argues this year's inflationary energy shock has accelerated the reckoning on public debt. It sees a slow squeeze where interest payments crowd out investment, defence and social spending, not a sudden replay of the euro crisis.
France is the focus for debt sustainability: weak growth, a large primary deficit and political gridlock. Italy has a higher debt ratio but runs a primary surplus and has more political stability.
Rabobank's base case is renewed Middle East escalation after the US midterms on 3 November, with fighting at varying intensity until end-Q1. It raises Brent to $120/bbl in Q1 and Q2 2027.
December Brent closed at $116.72/bbl on 29 October, the highest close since 29 April. The full-year 2027 swap is $92.41/bbl.
Persian Gulf-China tanker rates reached $1.4 million per day versus $40,000 normally, adding about $13.5/bbl to crude costs. The IEA puts total supply-chain costs at up to $37/bbl.

Global oil stocks are drawing by about 2-2.5 mb/d and refined products face a deficit of about 4 mb/d. About 12% of global refining capacity is offline. The US SPR is at 283 million barrels, the lowest since 1982.

Rabobank raised its Q4 2026 forecasts to EUR79/MWh for TTF and $25.40/MMBtu for JKM, assuming escalation in US military action against Iran. About 40 mtpa of non-Qatari LNG capacity could arrive in 2027 and about 50 mtpa more in 2028.

The ECB is not expected to hike as far as 2027 money market pricing implies. Rabobank forecasts EUR rates broadly stable through year-end. Lagarde said she sees no greater risk of second-round effects than in September.

Rabobank says the TPI is unlikely to be activated. If it were, it would be to shield other countries from French fallout, and the ECB may be less willing to support French yields until France adopts a fiscal plan. Further spread widening may be needed to force a budget compromise.
Eurozone Q3 GDP grew 0.4% q/q, with Ireland's 5.5% rise accounting for almost half. Rabobank raised 2026 growth to 1.0% and cut 2027 to 1.1%. It raised 2027 eurozone inflation to 3.9%.

Rabobank forecasts EUR/USD at 1.10 on a 3-month view, citing French and European political risk, energy costs and far-right gains. Le Pen is the front-runner in next spring's French presidential election.
Rabobank expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4.00% at Thursday's meeting, most likely 7-2, and again in February 2027. It sees the market pricing in too much BoE tightening and forecasts EUR/GBP at 0.84.
The UK Autumn Budget cut fiscal headroom to about GBP15bn from GBP23.6bn in March. Higher rates add about GBP14bn to debt servicing costs. Rabobank calls the plan not very credible.
Rabobank is constructive on JPY, with a 3-month USD/JPY forecast of 155.00 and a likely 25bp BoJ hike in December. It cites high domestic ownership of JGBs as a source of protection.

US CPI was 3.7% in September 2026 and unemployment is 4.2%, taking the misery index to 7.9%. Gasoline is $4.41 a gallon, up almost 37% since January 2025. Rabobank expects a Fed hike in December and then a hold through 2027.

Rabobank sees a Democratic win in at least one chamber as the main dividing line for US economic policy. That would mean fiscal gridlock, with a shutdown deadline on December 11 and a debt limit in 2027.
The Bank of Canada hiked 25bp to 2.50% on October 28. Rabobank expects at least one more hike in December and sees USD/CAD support near 1.385 and a range of 1.40-1.45.

Banxico is expected to hold at 6.50%. USD/MXN hit a one-year high of 18.8 and 3-month implied vol rose to about 11.1%. MXN net speculative longs fell from about 95k to about 10k, then recovered to above 20k.
In Brazil, Lula was re-elected with 51.8% of the vote. Rabobank expects the Selic to hold at 13.75% until March 2027 and cut to 12.00% by end-2027. It keeps USD/BRL at 5.35 at end-2026.

The PBOC moved to a 1.25% overnight reverse repo as the new benchmark rate from 2 November. Rabobank still expects one more 7-day RRR cut this year and revised USD/CNH to 6.65 at end-2026 and 6.50 at end-2027.
Rabobank expects the RBA to hike 25bp to 4.85% in November after Q3 CPI came in at 3.9% headline and 3.7% trimmed mean. It puts NAIRU at 5%.
Recent stress at several neoclouds and smaller hyperscalers led to higher credit risk premia and a pulled IPO. Rabobank reads this as a leverage concern, not a demand concern.

sector_views.rationale: Rabobank forecasts higher oil, refined product and gas prices on expected Middle East escalation and supply disruption.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest close since 29 April, as markets shift toward expecting prolonged disruption.

risk_factors: Further spread widening in French OATs if France fails to adopt corrective fiscal steps, with a risk of a liquidity crisis if investors lose all confidence.
Escalation in the Persian Gulf hitting oil, refined product and LNG flows, with diesel and marine fuel oil inventories possibly at new lows within ten weeks.
AI-related leverage at neoclouds and smaller hyperscalers, and competition between AI, defence and infrastructure spending and governments for capital.
UK fiscal credibility, since the Budget defers fiscal offsets until after the next general election.
Japan's debt near 200% of GDP and the risk of rising JGB yields.
Brazil fiscal slippage and unconvincing consolidation under the re-elected government, with the 40-hour workweek cutting about 0.7pp from 2027 GDP growth.
US government shutdown deadline on December 11 and the 2027 debt limit.
charts_described: Figure 1 shows the UK fiscal headroom for 2029-30 falling from GBP23.6bn in the March estimate to GBP15bn in the October estimate, with an underlying forecast of 14.5 and Budget effects of -11.1.
Eurozone Figure 3 plots the fiscal gap against debt, as % of GDP, for advanced economies, and Rabobank says the majority of governments need to cut to stabilise the debt ratio.
vol_and_positioning: USD/MXN 3-month implied vol rose to about 11.1%, 3.5 points above its September lows, after the lowest level since before the pandemic in August and September.
CFTC non-commercial MXN net longs fell from almost 95k in early September to about 10k in early October, a two-year low, then recovered to above 20k.
Rabobank notes the market prices at least two more Fed hikes by Q2 2027 and a USD/MXN forward above 19 on a six-month horizon.
geopolitical: Rabobank's base case is renewed escalation around Iran after the US midterms on 3 November. The US, Israel and a broader Arab and European coalition would attack Iran and the Houthis while defending Saudi Arabia, with fighting lasting until end-Q1.
Possible retaliation targets include Fujairah, the ADCOP bypass pipeline, Ras Laffan LNG, the Saudi East-West Pipeline, Ras Tanura, and potentially Egypt and the Suez Canal.
UKMTO reported 32 attacks in October versus 16 in September. The 'Hormuz Shuttle' moves tankers along Oman's coast under US air cover.
French political gridlock ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with Le Pen as front-runner, and the rise of the AfD in Germany.
The EU-UK summit on 20 November is expected to produce deals on agri-food trade, emissions trading, youth mobility and energy cooperation.
The 5th plenum in China purged 33 Central Committee members, 16 of them military. EU officials travel to Beijing in the week of 23 November to discuss renminbi valuation.
US midterm elections on 3 November, with polls and prediction markets pointing to a loss of unified Republican control.

tension_points.bull_case: Money market pricing for 2027 implies significant ECB hikes, and the ECB will not push back strongly while inflation risks stay to the upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions, weaker growth and French debt concerns, which drive safe haven flows that dampen yields, create a big hurdle for the ECB to hike as far as priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A visible improvement in the inflationary backdrop would let long-term rates come down, while a worse energy shock after the US midterms would keep risks to the upside.

tension_points.bull_case: Renewed escalation, infrastructure attacks and inventory depletion push Brent to $120/bbl in Q1 and Q2 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: New workarounds, additional production and meaningful de-escalation would take Brent to $108/bbl in Q3 and $92/bbl in Q4.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Meaningful de-escalation, or a credible prospect of it by late Q1, would undercut the high-price case.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher-for-longer energy keeps inflation high and the MPC hikes in November and again in February 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The market prices too much tightening, and a credible prospect of de-escalation by late Q1 could let the MPC look through high headline inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credible prospect of de-escalation by late Q1 would change the MPC's calculation.
